name: Kaansa
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: SIL (Showalter) orthography work implies unpublished phonology notes; only Miehe 2007 Gur classification cited

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en, fr) Kaansa language pages; fr page cites Équipe kaansa 2018, Guide de transition français-kaansa, SIL Ouagadougou (www.parlerkaansa.org)
sources.note: Tertiary: says Kaansa has four tones (high, low, rising, falling) marked by diacritics in the orthography; nothing on stress. parlerkaansa.org did not resolve (DNS) on 2026-09-17.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record for kaan1246 (meds: Showalter 2007 phonology or text collection; Miehe 1994 phonology or text collection; Labouret 1958 wordlist; Delafosse 1904 wordlist)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: Glottolog knows no grammar or phonology sketch of Kaansa, only two specific-feature papers and two old wordlists.

sources.citation: Showalter, Stuart D. 2007. Ghost consonants: the glottal stop in Kaansa. In Doris L. Payne & Jaime Peña (eds.), Selected Proceedings of the 37th Annual Conference on African Linguistics, 96-110. Somerville, MA: Cascadilla Proceedings Project.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Silent on stress. Whole paper is on the glottal stop; the only prosodic remark is fn. 1 (p. 96): 'Phonetic transcription is broad: a) only high tones and contour tones are marked..'. The word 'stressed' appears only inside a quotation from Hyman 1988 about other languages. Also notes (p. 98) that Kaansa contrasts short and long vowels.

sources.citation: Miehe, Gudrun & Kerstin Winkelmann (eds.). 2007. Noun class systems in Gur languages, vol. I: Southwestern Gur languages (without Gurunsi) (Gur Monographs / Monographies voltaïques 9). Köln: Rüdiger Köppe. Kaansa chapter (Miehe).

sources.note: Each chapter opens with a phonological overview (snippet shows a tone-system remark, 'three or four' tones); the fullest published morphophonological description of Kaansa. Would supersede nothing but is the best published sketch; check its phonology preamble for stress.
